summary: Final proposal: hand-typed grammar parser (factored phase+stack one-hot recurrent state) + router over 60 syntactic-situation experts of prefix->char tables reaches dev bpc 0.6790, top1 0.8075, 0 failures; parser UNK expert never routed.

Route counts: experts for modified objects of the clause after ', and' and for modified/nested relative-clause subjects inside objects receive 0 positions, consistent with an NP depth limit (depth>=2 NPs unmodified); encoding it improved bpc 0.6812 -> 0.6793.
Shrinking backoff/floor mass from 0.023 to 0.0012 lowered bpc 0.6919 -> 0.6819 with no new high-cost positions (worst position stays ~6 bits), since the grammar covers all dev text.
Length-based EOS term 6*tanh(0.6*(step-148.5)) on '.' (threshold from hand-counted doc lengths) cut after_period bpc from 0.081 to 0.031.

Remaining loss is near the entropy of the grammar (69% of bits at word starts, ~2.94 bpc there); further per-parameter tuning moves bpc by ~0.0005. A per-document latent complexity rate may exist but gain is estimated <=0.005 bpc.
